commercial_incentive: Yes - promotes collegeessayguy.com and asks for likes/subscribes to grow the channel
key_insights: Breaks down a real letter of continued interest line by line, identifying five components: an opening reaffirmation of interest (naming the school as top choice if true), 2-3 specific 'why us' moments referencing real campus experiences, bullet-pointed new information/updates since the original application, an optional mention of a campus visit with concrete details, and a closing thank-you

Recommends sending new, concrete updates (new honors, projects, published work) rather than just repeating enthusiasm, since deferral/waitlist reviewers are specifically looking for new information to shift a 'maybe' toward a 'yes'
Advises checking the specific instructions each school provides (email vs. form) rather than guessing, and to ask admissions directly if unsure

States effectiveness varies by school: schools with specific unmet institutional priorities that a student's letter happens to match can be meaningfully swayed, while schools that never dip into the waitlist may see no benefit at all
Advises against sending a letter if the school explicitly says not to, and suggests deciding based on whether the student would regret not sending one
notable_or_distinctive: Uses a full real example letter (to Yale) annotated point-by-point, showing not just what to include but why each specific sentence choice works rhetorically.
reliability_notes: General strategic advice presented as broadly applicable but honestly caveated as school-dependent ('maybe' it helps); no data on actual waitlist-conversion rates is provided, consistent with the genuine uncertainty of how much these letters matter.
